adjusted_prescription: The agent should be guided to consistently follow the left edge of the corridor when navigating around fires to reduce the risk of collisions and improve safety. This means the agent needs to prioritize hugging the left wall and avoid cutting through the middle areas where fires are often closer. Demonstrations should explicitly show this behavior by starting in setups where the left-edge path is clearly safer and more effective. These examples should highlight how maintaining this left-edge corridor strategy helps the agent generalize across different start and goal positions while avoiding dynamic fire hazards. By focusing on safe corridor hugging, the agent can better handle varied fire layouts without getting too close to dangerous tiles. It will also make the safety pattern more robust for real environments with unpredictable fire positions.
